# H008 — Both BUB1B candidate alleles are single-nucleotide substitutions at bi-allelic sites, so their submission spelling (chromosome, position, REF, ALT) is invariant under bcftools norm (left-alignment and multi-allelic splitting) and an exact-string scorer will match them as the callset spells them.

**Step:** [step-1](../README.md) — Does every variant in the callset have exactly one spelling, so that an exact-string-matching scorer can be trusted with an indel?
**Status:** supported  |  **Confidence:** 0.83  |  **Revisions:** 2
**Gene:** BUB1B  |  **Path:** scorer mechanics

## The claim

Both BUB1B candidate alleles are single-nucleotide substitutions at bi-allelic sites, so their submission spelling (chromosome, position, REF, ALT) is invariant under bcftools norm (left-alignment and multi-allelic splitting) and an exact-string scorer will match them as the callset spells them.

**Prediction if true.** For both alleles len(REF) = len(ALT) = 1 and the record carries a single ALT; running bcftools norm -m -both -f <GRCh38 no-chr FASTA> over the BUB1B locus leaves both records byte-identical in CHROM, POS, REF and ALT.

**What would refute it.** Either allele is an indel or sits in a multi-allelic record, or bcftools norm changes its POS, REF or ALT.

| 28 | neutral | 0.00 | absence | The 43,667 records on hs38d1 decoy contigs have no sequence in the reference used and were excluded; normalization is still a recorded run, not a tested pipeline stage. | `methodology/073` |
